title: Vikoma
summary: Appointment software for barbershops and salons, live in production. It replaces paper notebooks and double bookings.
description: I built it on my own for businesses in Ecuador. Beyond appointments, it covers client history, reference photos with consent under Ecuador's data protection law, WhatsApp booking confirmations, daily cash close, inventory and a waitlist. Feature modules have domain, application, infrastructure and UI layers; scheduling rules are pure functions tested without a database.
challenges: One business could reference another business's data: tenant isolation relied on foreign keys, and the newer tursodb engine silently ignored them.
Concurrent writes, such as two checkouts at the same time, could sell stock that no longer existed or assign the same invoice number twice.
The OAuth sign-in check accepted any value as valid: a hex parser read base64url input and returned empty buffers, so every comparison matched.
solutions: I confirmed it with an insert that should have failed, moved production to libSQL, and made the app refuse to boot when foreign keys are not enforced.

Invoice numbers come from an atomic UPDATE with RETURNING, tested with 25 concurrent requests that must get 25 different numbers. Stock changes use conditional updates as guards against overselling, and lock errors are retried.
A negative security test caught it, and I replaced the check with a constant-time comparison that hashes both sides first.
